news.title: 4 Takeaways From Freedom 250 & American Kyle Kirkwood's Victory
news.text: Washington — Kyle Kirkwood, who has been the best U.S.-born driver in INDYCAR the last two seasons, made him a popular winner of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix — an event designed to celebrate the country’s 250th anniversary season. The Andretti Global driver led 128 of the 147 laps of a race where President Donald Trump waved the green flag and the drivers competed on a 1.7-mile circuit that included Pennsylvania Avenue as well as Constitution and Independence within view of many iconic U.S. landmarks. "America is built on many different nations," Andretti Global driver Kyle Kirkwood told me Sunday night. "In many ways, I don’t believe that today had to be won by an American. It just so happened that we were the best car out there today and we did everything right and were the winners. "In many ways I’m glad because I think that there’s a lot of people that are here as fans or watching on TV that wanted to see an American win. I’m glad I could give them that satisfaction, but it’s not easy to win any INDYCAR race, and the fact I was able to do it today as an American is a massive deal." Here are my takeaways: With no huge issues with the track and no security breaches, the event went off without a major hitch. That was a major accomplishment for a race that was put together in late January when a Trump executive order gave INDYCAR the access to fast-track permits it needed. Trump stayed for the entire event and several members of his cabinet and other legislators were in attendance. Organizers said that 215,000 fans came to the grounds during the two days, many on free tickets. The president took a photo with past INDYCAR champions and Indianapolis 500 winners. "For me, being from a small town in Australia, to end up standing and talking to an American president is surreal," Will Power said in his post-race news conference. "It’s something I never would have dreamed of. "It was just incredible to stand there, talk to the president and the First Lady, then jump in a race car and race in Washington, D.C." Andretti Global didn’t just snag the victory, it also had Will Power finishing third and Marcus Ericsson finishing fourth. Only Arrow McLaren’s Christian Lundgaard, who placed second, broke up the Andretti Global party. "The team has made huge progression over this season, and you can see it now," Power said in his post-race news conference. "It's all coming online. I think the expectation now every weekend is to be on the podium — challenge for a win." Scott McLaughlin tried to make the pass on Kirkwood on a restart for the lead with 19 laps remaining. It ended with McLaughlin with a wrecked race car. "It was hard to pass all day," McLaughlin told me after the accident. "I saw an opportunity. He braked really early, and obviously it was the right move from him to brake that early. But I thought that was my chance to make a move. "I just locked the rears late, and once I locked the rears, I was toast. That was my opportunity. I went for it. And I don’t regret it." Four-time INDYCAR champion Alex Palou finished three laps down in 20th, seeing his championship lead go from 133 ahead of Kirkwood to 91. That is still a big lead with three races left in the season, and Palou very well could clinch next weekend at the doubleheader at The Milwaukee Mile. As he was exiting the pits, Palou hit a tire that was being set to be put on Mick Schumacher’s car, resulting in a pass-through penalty. And then he bent a toe link when he tapped the wall, a toe link that eventually broke and he ended up in the wall. "It was one of those days where I did a couple of mistakes," Palou told me and another reporter after the race. "We had a bad stop. We had everything happening to us today. "I prefer this than having it spread out in different races." INDYCAR will have a doubleheader weekend at The Milwaukee Mile, where it will race both Saturday and Sunday. Both races will be 250 laps. As far as short ovals, there have been two this year — both won by Josef Newgarden.
news.summary: American Kyle Kirkwood got into Winner's Circle at the Freedom 250, but reigning INDYCAR champion Alex Palou had a day to forget in D.C.

news.title: A new American view of Kashmir as integral part of India - Daily Excelsior
news.text: T N AshokUS Envoy Sergio Gor's visit to Srinagar describing J&K as an integral part of India is a moment that redefines US government perception of the decades old Indo Pak dispute on Kashmir as his choice of words about India's sovereignty over the region goes far beyond terming it as one of the most beautiful places he has ever seen. Jammu and Kashmir, Gor said, was an "important part of India."For a territory that has been at the centre of seven decades of Indian-Pakistani rivalry, the words were unusually direct. They were also followed by something more tangible: Gor said Washington would review its travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, raising the prospect that the United States could finally lower the highest warning it has maintained for the region.The distinction matters. The U.S. State Department calls its warning Level 4 - "Do Not Travel," not a "D-level" threat. The warning has covered Jammu and Kashmir because of terrorism and civil unrest and has specifically identified Srinagar, Gulmarg and Pahalgam as places where violence could occur.Gor's visit therefore comes at an intriguing moment. The question is no longer simply whether Kashmir is safe enough for American tourists. It is whether Washington's assessment of Kashmir's political and security environment is beginning to catch up with the transformation India says has taken place on the ground.Gor said he had been impressed by the security arrangements put in place by the central and Jammu and Kashmir governments and by the systems designed to protect ordinary people. That is important because the American advisory is not merely a travel brochure's warning. It is a formal assessment of risk by the world's most powerful diplomatic and intelligence establishment. If that assessment changes, the consequences will extend beyond tourism.American tourists have never been a large component of Kashmir's foreign-tourist market. In 2019, according to data cited from the Jammu and Kashmir Crime Investigation Department, about 26,662 foreign tourists from 106 countries visited the Valley; Americans numbered approximately 731. That makes the American traveller a useful barometer rather than a major source of tourist revenue. The broader tourism numbers tell a more dramatic story. Kashmir has moved from years in which militancy and shutdowns kept visitors away to a period of extraordinary mass tourism. Jammu and Kashmir recorded about 2.36 crore tourist visits in 2024, while the number of foreign visitors rose to more than 65,000.Yet Washington continued to tell Americans not to go. Indeed, the Level 4 warning predates Donald Trump's return to the White House. In July 2024, the State Department placed Jammu and Kashmir at Level 4, citing terrorism and civil unrest. The Pahalgam massacre of April 2025, in which 26 people were killed, mostly tourists, gave Washington an even stronger reason to retain the warning. That makes Gor's intervention more significant. He is not simply announcing that Kashmir has become picturesque again. He is suggesting that the security equation deserves another look.Why Washington may be changing its calculation; The most obvious reason is the changed security environment. Since the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019, New Delhi has pursued an aggressive strategy of suppressing militant networks, tightening intelligence coordination and expanding physical security around tourist centres. The restoration of mass tourism became one of the most visible indicators of that effort.But the Pahalgam attack exposed the limits of declaring victory. The killing of tourists demonstrated that even a heavily secured tourist economy could be penetrated. What appears to have impressed Gor is something slightly different: the capacity of the state to respond.A security assessment is rarely based on whether a place has experienced violence. It asks whether governments can prevent attacks, respond to them, protect foreigners and restore order when something goes wrong. Gor's comments suggest that American officials are examining precisely those capabilities.There is another reason. Washington's strategic relationship with New Delhi has changed dramatically. India is no longer viewed in Washington simply through the prism of its relationship with Pakistan. It is an increasingly important strategic partner in the Indo-Pacific, a defence partner and a counterweight to China.Kashmir consequently has less room to remain an isolated India-Pakistan problem in American strategic thinking. That does not mean Washington has formally abandoned its longstanding position that Kashmir is disputed. The current State Department advisory still describes the territory as disputed among India, Pakistan and China. But Gor's language about Jammu and Kashmir being an important part of India represents a striking diplomatic emphasis.The episode has a recent precedent. In February, the U.S. Trade Representative's office published a map of India that showed Pakistan-administered Kashmir and Aksai Chin within Indian territory. It was striking because Washington had traditionally avoided cartographic formulations that appeared to endorse India's territorial claims. The map disappeared from the USTR's social-media account within days. The deletion restored the ambiguity. Gor's statement, however, cannot simply be deleted from the diplomatic record.Together, the two episodes suggest a Washington wrestling with two impulses: avoiding unnecessary confrontation with Pakistan while simultaneously accommodating India's insistence that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of the country.The roots lie in the chaotic autumn of 1947. At Partition, the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir had the option of acceding to either India or Pakistan. Maharaja Hari Singh initially hesitated. In October, armed tribesmen and Pakistani nationals entered Kashmir. Hari Singh sought Indian military assistance and signed the Instrument of Accession to India. Indian troops were flown into Srinagar and pushed back the attackers.This is where the Indian narrative of Nehru's "mistake" begins. Critics argue that Jawaharlal Nehru should have allowed the Indian Army to continue its advance until the entire princely state was recovered instead of accepting a ceasefire and taking the dispute to the United Nations. They regard the decision as having frozen a battlefield problem into an international dispute.The historical reality is more complicated. Nehru acted amid British military influence, the advice of Governor-General Lord Mountbatten and the danger of a wider India-Pakistan war. India went to the United Nations in January 1948. The Security Council subsequently adopted Resolution 47, which called first for Pakistan to secure the withdrawal of tribesmen and Pakistani nationals who had entered Kashmir to fight, followed by conditions for a plebiscite.The crucial first step was never completed. The ceasefire line eventually hardened into what became the Line of Control, LoC, leaving Pakistan administering the territory it calls "Azad Jammu and Kashmir" and India calling it Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Seven decades later, the unresolved geography remains.The irony across the Line of Control; The latest irony is that the sharpest political discontent may now be emerging inside Pakistan-administered Kashmir itself.For years, Islamabad presented "Azad Kashmir" as the liberated alternative to Indian-administered Kashmir. But the region has witnessed sustained protests over electricity prices, shortages of subsidised wheat, political representation and what residents describe as excessive influence by Pakistan's political and military establishment.The grievances have a striking economic logic. Mangla Dam, built in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, transformed the region's rivers into a major source of electricity for Pakistan. Residents have argued that a territory bearing the environmental and social costs of major hydroelectric projects should not have to pay high electricity tariffs for power generated from its own resources. The Joint Awami Action Committee has become the vehicle for much of this discontent.The unrest has increasingly become a challenge to Pakistan's political management of the territory. Elections in 2026 were accompanied by violence, clashes and allegations of political manipulation. Reuters reported more than 30 deaths in clashes around the regional election period. (IPA)

news.title: Kyle Kirkwood Gives Freedom 250 an American Winner on the Streets of Downtown Washington
news.text:
WASHINGTON—On the streets of downtown Washington, an American led almost the whole way.

Kyle Kirkwood raced to his second victory of the IndyCar season Sunday, dominating the Freedom 250 in his No. 27 Honda. Kirkwood crossed the finish line in front of the U.S. Capitol 3.09 seconds ahead of Christian Lundgaard, after leading for 128 of a possible 147 laps.

“This likely is the most satisfying win that I’ve had, just the magnitude of it. This one and my first are pretty similar,” said Kirkwood, who now has seven career IndyCar victories. “When you think about the magnitude, what this means, having this race here in D.C., being the Freedom 250, as an American, it might top the first win for me.”

The race was set up as part of the country’s 250th birthday celebration. President Donald Trump gave drivers the green flag at the start and District of Columbia Mayor Muriel Bowser served as grand marshal.

Organizers could hardly have asked for better weather, with plenty of sun but not so much heat that fans would stay away. The area was awash in red, white and blue. Even the Canadian flags on that country’s embassy—located along the track’s Pennsylvania Avenue straightaway—featured two of those three colors.

“This was not a race. It was an event,” race chair Bud Denker said.

Will Power and Marcus Ericsson, Kirkwood’s teammates with Andretti Global, finished third and fourth. Pole winner Alex Palou, who had a chance to clinch the series title, finished 20th in his second-worst showing of the year.

After several prerace flyovers and Trump’s green flag, the field quickly went under caution because of debris on the track. The first big wreck came when David Malukas went into the wall and Sting Ray Robb could do little to avoid crashing into him coming around a turn. Just like that, two of the race’s eight American drivers were out.

Several cars went onto pit road, and that’s when the day started to fall apart for Palou. He appeared to hit a tire in someone else’s area while exiting, and he was assessed a drive-through penalty.

On a subsequent pit stop, one of Palou’s tires was loose when he started driving. That caused another delay, and he ended up off the lead lap. Palou later spun coming through a turn. His lead in the standings dropped from 133 points over second-place Kirkwood to 91 with three races to go.

“Things happen. I’m at least kind of happy that everything happened at the same day instead of spreading out throughout different races,” Palou said. “We had some issues in pit lane — one my fault, one out of my control.”

Kirkwood had a commanding lead before Palou’s spin caused a caution. On a restart with 19 laps remaining, Scott McLaughlin tried to pass Kirkwood and went into a tire barrier.

“Quite honestly, I thought he was going to make it stick initially,” Kirkwood said. “Once he got alongside me, there’s no way he’s stopping.”

After another caution, Kirkwood pulled off a strong restart with 13 laps to go and Lundgaard didn’t mount much of a threat as the 250-mile race wound down. Nicknamed the “King of the Streets” because of his success on tracks like this, Kirkwood looked right at home on the 1.7-mile circuit that was being used this weekend for the first time.

Marcus Armstrong was penalized for avoidable contact when he sent Christian Rasmussen into a spin. Rinus VeeKay went into the wall during that incident but appeared unaware of Armstrong’s culpability when he went on TV for an interview.

“If Rasmussen’s around, you know you’re going to crash. Either he does or you do,” VeeKay said. “It sucks. It’s stupid. It’s a long race, and some people seemingly don’t know that.”

Denker had plenty of impressive stats ready for his postrace news conference: over 215,000 people attending over the last two days, and over $969,000 in merchandise sold Saturday.

As for whether the race will continue in the future, Denker said he'll discuss it with series owner Roger Penske.

“Mr. Trump hit me 15 times today about having to have this,” Denker said. “‘Let’s do it for five years,’ is what he’s saying, ‘because that guarantees you’re going to be here through my term, then two more years for whoever is in office next.’”

news.title: "Vessels violating Iranian protocols for Strait of Hormuz" shall face fines, detention, confiscation: Iran
news.text:
Tehran [Iran], August 24 (ANI): Iran's Ports and Maritime Organization (PGSA) has warned vessels violating its protocols for the Strait of Hormuz that they could face restrictions on future passages, including fines, detention or confiscation.In a post on X on Monday, PGSA said, "Vessels violating Iranian protocols for the Strait of Hormuz shall face restrictions on future passages, including fines, detention, or confiscation."

1/Vessels violating Iranian protocols for the #Strait_of_Hormuz shall face restrictions on future passages, including fines, detention, or confiscation. https://t.co/B8BWeitpzh— PGSA | نهاد مدیریت آبراه خلیج فارس (@PGSA_IRAN) August 23, 2026

The authority also warned that vessels cooperating with ships already listed as non-compliant would themselves be added to the list."Effective immediately, any vessel cooperating with listed vessels (via STS, transshipment, etc.) will be added to the list," PGSA said.It urged cargo owners shipping to or from the Persian Gulf to review its Non-Compliant Vessels (NCV) list before chartering vessels to avoid potential issues."Prior to chartering, cargo owners shipping to/from the #Persian_Gulf must review the Non-Compliant Vessels (NCV) list at [http://pgsa.ir/non-compliant-vessels-list/](http://pgsa.ir/non-compliant-vessels-list/) in order to avoid potential issues," it said.PGSA said vessels seeking removal from the list must submit a formal application along with justifications."To request removal, vessels must submit a formal application with justifications to [[email protected]](mailto:[email protected])," the authority said.Earlier, Iran on Sunday said that vessels from "authorised" countries transiting the Strait of Hormuz will now be required to pay service fees to Tehran.Detailing the scope of the decision, Iran's National Security Commission Spokesperson Ebrahim Rezaei stated that the fees will cover a wide range of maritime, environmental, and logistical provisions.According to state broadcaster IRIB, this comes after the approval of the Article 3 "Strategic Action to Ensure the Security and Progress of the Strait of Hormuz" plan."Article 3 of the 'Strategic Action to Ensure the Security and Progress of the Strait of Hormuz' plan was approved by the National Security Commission, according to which ships from countries authorised to pass through the Strait of Hormuz will pay for the services provided by Iran," he said."Fees will be charged for services including navigation, environmental, fueling under certain conditions, insurance, safety and other services we provide," he added.The spokesperson further stated that the payment structures have been designed with flexible financial terms."These fees will be charged in Rials or any other currency desired by the Islamic Republic of Iran," IRIB cited him as saying.Meanwhile, Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), Mohsen Rezaei, on Saturday (local time) said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and will not reopen until the United States fulfils its commitments and changes its behaviour amid escalating tensions between Tehran and Washington.In an interview with IRIB, Rezaei said, "The Strait of Hormuz is closed, despite American claims, and will not open until America corrects its behaviour.""This time, America must first fulfil its obligations," he added.On the other hand, US President Donald Trump reiterated his claim of US control over the critical waterway by sharing an image that depicts the Strait of Hormuz as "NEW US Territory."The latest post on Truth Social follows Trump's earlier sharing of the identical graphic on August 18, after he previously floated the prospect of claiming jurisdiction over the waterway. (ANI)

news.title: Soccer-UEFA's Ceferin says Infantino could face election challenger, rules out FIFA bid
news.text:
Aug 23 (Reuters) - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin ruled himself ⁠out of running for the FIFA presidency but said Gianni Infantino would likely face a challenger if he ⁠seeks reelection next year following a global backlash over a plan to sell part of the World Cup ‌to private investors. 

Speaking to "The Rest Is Politics: Leading" podcast, which will air on Monday, Ceferin said he was not interested in succeeding Infantino despite growing uncertainty around the FIFA president's future after his abandoned investment proposal.

"One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at ​a certain point you have also, I mean, it's time also to enjoy ⁠life a bit," Ceferin said. 

"Let's see till when. ⁠And the second point is, my credibility is much, much, much higher if I'm not interested in the position."

news.title: Wary Of Backlash, Pro-Israel GOP Senate Hopeful Asks AIPAC Not To Spend On His Behalf
news.text:
With Israel's standing in the United States crumbling, America's leading pro-Israel organization has become a focal point of anger among those who think the US government is putting Israel's interests ahead of America's. Political candidates have started seizing on this, attacking opponents who are backed by that group -- AIPAC. So for, that's largely been a phenomenon in the Democratic primaries, but now -- in a jarring indication of AIPAC's ballot-box toxicity -- staunchly pro-Israel GOP Senate hopeful Mike Rogers has asked AIPAC not to spend money on his general election campaign. 

Rogers, a former US representative who chaired the House intelligence committee from 2011 to 2015, has been a stalwart backer of US aid to Israel, and was one of 12 federal legislators honored in 2015 by the US-Israel Security Alliance for his work to arm the Israel Defense Forces. 

Having won the Republican primary, Rogers faces Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed in the general election. El-Sayed is an outspoken critic of Israel and US support for Israel, which is why AIPAC blew through $30 million in a failed attempt to secure the Democratic nomination for the Israel-catering Haley Stevens. In that campaign, El-Sayed deftly portrayed Stevens as beholden to Israel. Stevens had given him all the ammo he needed; indeed, the El-Sayed campaign created a website that did nothing but show this cringy Stevens performance on a continuous loop: 

Rep. Haley Stevens: "In the United States Congress, I will continue to fight for the people of Israel!"
"Israel comes to me in my dreams!" pic.twitter.com/flVVYp3EWP
— AIPAC Tracker (@TrackAIPAC) June 9, 2026

When his primary victory was nearly in hand, El-Sayed taunted AIPAC, saying, "AIPAC, if you're listening, come back and burn it again" in the general election. AIPAC was poised to start running an already-produced commercial for the November race when Rogers talked to AIPAC chair Michael Tuchin in Los Angeles last week, Axios reports. The next day, the commercial was put on ice. 

The extraordinary move by the Rogers campaign is a humiliation for AIPAC, which has long been nearly omnipotent in securing lopsided congressional votes on pro-Israel bills, and in installing pro-Israel legislators while ousting those who dare to offer even mild criticism of Israel. While AIPAC has hit "pause" on its effort in the Michigan Senate campaign, angry AIPAC officials want back in. 

Rogers' allies are urging AIPAC to use indirect ways to influence the race, so that AIPAC's backing isn't used against Rogers. One technique under discussion is telling AIPAC donors to give their money to a pro-Rogers super PAC rather than AIPAC, Axios reported. The Rogers team has also floated the idea of directly hiring AIPAC's political strategists. However, not wanting to own up to the fact that it has become political poison, AIPAC wants a visible role in the race, with hopes of notching a big win that reinforces the group's power as other politicians stake out their positions on Israel. Things have gotten so icy between the Rogers camp and AIPAC that other GOP players are attempting to intermediate, including Jewish Republican donors. 

According to a recent Fox News poll, 55% of the Michigan electorate want US aid to Israel to stop altogether. The state has one of the larger Arab American populations, and from election to election, it's demonstrated mobility across the Red-Blue divide. Outraged over the Biden administration's blank-check support for Israel's devastation of Gaza, the most heavily-Arab precincts in east Dearborn went for the self-described "peace candidate" Donald Trump in 2024, with 45% voting for Trump, 29% for the Green Party's Jill Stein, and only 16% for Biden's VP Kamala Harris.

news.title: U.S. Plans Tougher Iran Sanctions, Bessent Says
news.text:
Scott Bessent, United States Secretary of the Treasury, said Washington intends to impose what he described as the "toughest sanctions in history” against Iran and launch an unprecedented coordinated financial isolation campaign aimed at cutting economic lifelines available to the Iranian government.



Speaking to CNBC, Bessent said President Donald Trump’s administration was calling on U.S. allies and other countries to stop trading with Iran. He warned that Washington would use its economic leverage against governments and entities that decline to comply with the sanctions campaign.



Bessent said countries continuing to support Iran economically risk international isolation, arguing that sustained financial pressure could reduce the need for additional military force. He also warned that Trump would respond rapidly if Iran attacked American forces or neighboring countries.



The Treasury secretary has linked the pressure campaign to energy markets, saying tougher measures could eventually lower oil prices. He specifically highlighted China, describing Beijing as a major purchaser of Iranian petroleum and arguing that participation in Washington’s initiative would serve Chinese economic interests.



The United States has already imposed restrictions targeting Iran’s energy, maritime and financial sectors. Washington has also sought to disrupt revenue channels it says enable Tehran to maintain access to international markets despite existing sanctions.



Trump recently described the planned measures as an exceptionally severe economic campaign and warned of consequences for countries maintaining significant commercial relations with Iran. Bessent is scheduled to provide further details of the measures at a Monday news conference.



Iranian officials have responded with warnings of their own. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said any country participating in economic restrictions against Iran would be regarded as an enemy.



"If Trump takes any action against Iran, our confrontation will be like an earthquake,” Rezaei said. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei separately characterized Washington’s planned measures as an attempt to impose authority beyond U.S. borders.



The escalating economic confrontation comes amid continuing hostilities dating from February and tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic passage for international energy shipments. Diplomatic efforts have continued alongside the confrontation, but no new settlement has been announced.



The effectiveness of Washington’s strategy will depend significantly on compliance by Iran’s major commercial partners. Attempts to penalize third-country trade could widen the dispute beyond Washington and Tehran, placing governments and companies under growing pressure to choose between Iranian commercial ties and access to U.S.-linked financial markets.

news.title: CNN Panel Erupts as Scott Jennings Defends Trump Aide Natalie Harp
news.text:
CNN commentator Scott Jennings faced pushback on Wednesday’s episode of NewsNight, where fellow panelists accused him of manufacturing outrage over remarks Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff made about White House aide Natalie Harp.

Ossoff, taking aim at Trump on Sunday, said the president appeared “less interested” in doing the job and more eager to “travel with” his 35-year-old executive assistant “to their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar.”

Jennings argued that the comment unfairly dragged Harp, whom he described as largely unknown to the public, into a national political fight.

“She’s not a household name, nobody knows who she is, and when he injected her into this, he knew what he was doing, which is punching down on someone who’s effectively defenseless,” Jennings said.

ABC News chief legal analyst Dan Abrams quickly challenged that line of criticism, asking: “Doesn’t Donald Trump do that all the time?”

Florida Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz was even more forceful, arguing that Trump had already “broke all the rules” when he celebrated longtime critic Rob Reiner following the director’s death late last year.

“What I find amazing is that the best trolls can’t take incoming. I don’t care who they are,” Moskowitz said. Jennings immediately pushed back, asking, “Is she a troll?” in reference to Harp.

The exchange quickly grew heated, with Jennings and Moskowitz talking over each other as the CNN NewsNight panel tried to unpack the controversy.

Moskowitz maintained, ‘No, but Trump is.’

Jennings, shouting over his co-panelist, framed Harp as a ‘female who can’t defend herself.’

‘She’s a White House staff member,’ former Bill Clinton aide Keith Boykin blurted out. 

‘It’s a single defenseless woman,’ said Jennings.

The crosstalk grew so chaotic that host Abby Phillip – also the show’s moderator – felt the need to jump in. 

‘Hold on a sec,’ she repeated several times with a smile.

Moskowitz, meanwhile, shouted that whenever CNN Chief White House Correspondent Kaitlan Collins ‘asks a real question’ President Trump ‘demeans her every single solitary day.’

Phillip then cued a sequence of clips she felt opposed Jennings’ argument, framing it as evidence of ‘Trump punching down on women.’

Included was Trump acknowledging to Megyn Kelly his belief that Rosie O’Donnell was a ‘disgusting animal’ during the first Republican presidential primary in 2015 and slamming Hillary Clinton as ‘a nasty woman’ on a different debate stage the following year. 

The footage was rounded out by Trump telling Kaitlan Collins to ‘smile’ in February and Bloomberg’s White House correspondent Catherine Lucey to ‘Quiet, piggy,’ this past November. 

‘Quiet, piggy,’ Phillip emphasized. ‘I mean, Scott. Dan’s question was pretty straightforward. If you’re going to be outraged over traveling on a plane with Natalie, are you going to be outraged over all those things?’

Harp – Trump’s personal assistant since 2022 – began making headlines several days before being named in Ossoff’s speech, after a Washington Post report pegged her as one of the few allowed on a secret flight with the President out of Turkey last month amid an Iranian assassination threat.

‘I do not believe in demeaning women in any way. Number one,’ Jennings shot back. 

A Politico report the following day claimed Jennings sent clips of his recent on-air Harp defenses to the White House in a bid to succeed outgoing Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt.

As he got to ‘number two’, Phillip and others repeatedly urged him to answer her question. Jennings refused.

‘By the way, you don’t know how loud this is,’ he said, referring to pushback from Boykin.

‘You have no idea how dishonest you are,’ the former Clinton aide proclaimed.

As Jennings urged fellow conservative Lydia Moynihan to get involved, Phillip again took over. 

‘Just to be clear, I think the idea of continually describing a 35-year-old woman as somebody who has no agency and is defenseless and is just a victim, that is kind of demeaning,’ she said.

The exchange ended shortly thereafter.

The day before, CNN’s Erin Burnett hosted Harp’s estranged brother Preston Harp on her show ‘OutFront.’ 

Preston framed his sister’s relationship with Trump as a ‘unhealthy obsession,’ after CNN reported she jumped into an SUV trunk just to accompany Trump to a New York federal court building in 2023. 

The Post report sparked questions about Trump’s closeness with the staffer, enough so that The New York Times profiled her on Tuesday. 

Her devotion to Trump has remained consistent throughout the years despite attempts by his inner circle to distance her from the President, according to the Times and CNN.

news.title: Syria holds talks with Israel addressing de-escalation and Israel-Turkey tensions
news.text:
Syria said it held talks with Israel in Jordan on Sunday on de-escalation after recent Israeli strikes, and on keeping the country out of tensions between Israel and Turkey, an ally of Damascus.
The high-level negotiations came after the sides in January agreed to establish an intelligence-sharing mechanism as they edge towards a security agreement.
They also came after Israel bombed the disused Abu Duhur airbase in the country’s northwest earlier in the week, claiming it wanted to avert Turkish troops deploying to the facility. Ankara denied any visit to the site.
Syrian state news agency SANA quoted a diplomatic source at the foreign ministry saying “a high-level Syrian delegation headed by the foreign minister and including the general and military intelligence chiefs” met a high-level Israeli delegation “under American mediation and hosted by Jordan”.
The meeting was “part of efforts aiming at de-escalation after recent Israeli bombardment of Syrian territory, escalating tensions in southern Syria, and in support of stability in Syria and the region”, said the source.
Discussions also addressed “efforts aimed at bringing closer the viewpoints between Turkey and Israel and ensuring the current tension between the two countries are not reflected on Syria territory”, the report added.
A diplomatic source and a Syrian government source told Agence France-Presse that Foreign Minister Assad al-Shaibani met the head of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency Roman Gofman.
They discussed issues such as establishing “a special operations room” in Jordan under US supervision to prevent any confrontation in Syria, including involving Turkey, the sources added.

US envoy for Syria Tom Barrack had slammed Israel’s attack on the airbase on Tuesday as an “unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability”.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan have traded barbs since the incident, with tensions high between the two leaders.
The Syrian government source told Agence France-Presse that Sunday’s talks were the first between Israel and Syria in some time, while the diplomatic source said they were the first in several months.
SANA said the discussions addressed “establishing practical mechanisms to stop Israeli attacks … and reviving the negotiations process with the aim of reaching a security agreement that could form the basis of a more comprehensive future agreement”.
Israel and Syria’s new authorities have held several rounds of direct talks, and after negotiations in Paris in January they agreed to establish a dedicated communication cell under US supervision to lower bilateral tensions.
An Arab diplomat in Damascus said at the time that a joint operations room based in Jordan would follow issues including security co-ordination and border control.

Israel has launched hundreds of strikes on Syria since the December 2024 toppling of long-time ruler Bashar al-Assad by Islamist forces it considers jihadists.
It sent troops into a UN-patrolled buffer zone that had long separated Israeli and Syrian forces on the Israeli-annexed Golan Heights.
Israel has also carried out repeated incursions deeper into Syrian territory and has vowed to keep troops in a so-called security zone in southern Syria, where it seeks a broader demilitarised area.
The talks also came a day after Israel struck what it said was a militant in southern Syria. Damascus said one person was wounded in the strike, which it called a “flagrant violation” of its sovereignty.
Israel captured most of the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 Arab-Israeli War and later annexed the areas under its control, a move only recognised by the United States and, this month, Colombia.
US President Donald Trump has been pushing for a security deal between Syria and Israel but Israel remains distrustful of Syria’s authorities.

news.title: Greece moves Patriot battery to Crete as Iran threatens US bases in Europe
news.text: After the Iranian threat, Bulgaria announced that two U.S. refueling aircraft had been evacuated from the country — but Greece is instead bolstering its defenses: According to reports in Greece, the country has moved a Patriot air defense battery from the island of Karpathos to Crete to strengthen defenses around the Souda Bay area in northwestern Crete, which is considered strategically important. The battery, including personnel and equipment, was moved overnight and is expected to be deployed near the military base at Souda. According to Greek reports, the decision was made following threats by senior Iranian officials against U.S. bases in Europe, while Greek military forces remain on heightened alert. Assessments indicate that Iran still has a significant number of ballistic missiles with ranges exceeding 2,000 kilometers (1,240 miles), putting targets in southeastern Europe within their reach. The Patriot battery was deployed to Karpathos in March as part of Greece’s efforts to strengthen its defenses against ballistic missile threats. According to the report, Athens is in contact with the United States and Israel regarding potential threats to facilities in Greece and Cyprus and is also considering helping Bulgaria’s air defense system if an official request is received. The close ties between Greece and Israel, including in the face of threats from Turkey, have been reported on numerous occasions in the past. Bulgaria, meanwhile, announced Saturday that two U.S. military refueling aircraft whose deployment at Bezmer Air Base in southeastern Bulgaria last month had angered Iran were evacuated and moved to another location. The announcement by Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov came several days after the British Financial Times reported that Iran was considering targeting U.S. assets in southeastern Europe, including Bulgaria and Cyprus, in the event of renewed escalation with the United States. Bulgaria approved the deployment of two KC-135 military aircraft a month ago. The aircraft are among those used to refuel fighter jets, including on their way to carry out strikes in Iran. Sofia has consistently insisted that the aircraft deployed on its territory were used only for training missions in the airspace of allied countries and not for strikes against Iran, which are not currently taking place amid the tense pause in fighting with the United States. Iran, however, reacted sharply, claiming that the presence of U.S. military aircraft in the country made Bulgaria a partner in “aggression and war crimes.” Meanwhile, following U.S. President Donald Trump’s declaration of an “economic D-Day” against Iran, Tehran has continued its verbal attacks while the situation on the ground remains relatively quiet. Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said the U.S. president’s remarks “about economic warfare are a tacit admission of the humiliating defeat in the military arena. If you had won on the military front, you would not have needed to launch an economic war. We have a scenario for every hostile action by the enemy. There is no concern on the economic front.” Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf took a jab at the U.S. announcements that talks had been frozen in a post on X: “What’s the plan for bonds, import frozen yields? Frozen homebuyers for housing? Frozen paychecks for wages? A frozen foreign policy delivers a frozen economy. The only thing still moving? The Iran boomerang.” But while the Twitter battles continue, Iran’s economic crisis is becoming increasingly apparent. The U.S. dollar reached an exchange rate of 2 million rials on Iran’s free market, crossing a threshold it had approached in recent days. According to Iran International, the dollar traded at around 1.865 million rials at the beginning of last week, meaning it rose by more than 7% in less than a week. In just one year, it has more than doubled in value, after trading at 958,000 rials during the same period last year. Just last week, President Masoud Pezeshkian, a relatively moderate figure within the regime but one considered to have limited influence, again called for an end to the war. In remarks quoted by Iranian media, Pezeshkian said his government was “trying to solve the problems” currently facing Iran’s economy. He added: “During this period, despite all the problems, we have had many achievements that have not been addressed. We do not deny the shortcomings and deficiencies, but we are trying to move the country forward.”
news.summary: Greece moved a Patriot air defense battery to Crete amid Iranian threats to US bases in Europe and is considering helping Bulgaria strengthen its air defenses if Sofia makes a formal request

news.title: Canadá respalda a Carney ante guerra comercial con Estados Unidos  - Puerto Rico Tribune – Daily Puerto Rico
news.text:
Los sindicatos también respaldaron la postura del Ejecutivo. Unifor, el mayor sindicato del sector privado canadiense y con fuerte presencia en la industria automotriz, aseguró que los negociadores hicieron “lo correcto” al abandonar la mesa y reclamó represalias estratégicas contra Washington.

El respaldo se extiende a comentaristas políticos y económicos del país, que sostienen que aceptar las últimas exigencias estadounidenses habría supuesto sacrificar parte de la soberanía canadiense sin garantizar estabilidad en la relación comercial.

Canadá se prepara para una confrontación prolongada

La disputa abre ahora un escenario de incertidumbre para la economía canadiense. Los nuevos aranceles estadounidenses del 50 por ciento, vigentes desde la medianoche del sábado, afectan unos 28,000 millones de dólares canadienses en exportaciones, equivalentes a cerca de 20,000 millones de dólares estadounidenses, principalmente en el sector manufacturero.

Como respuesta, Ottawa anunció que impondrá represalias arancelarias “dólar por dólar” a partir del próximo 8 de septiembre.

El Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) estima que las nuevas tarifas podrían restar alrededor de cuatro décimas al Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) canadiense. Entre los sectores más expuestos se encuentran la electrónica, los textiles, los muebles, la madera y el papel.

El sector empresarial canadiense, aunque respalda la decisión de evitar un acuerdo considerado desfavorable, ha advertido que la incertidumbre comercial podría frenar inversiones y prolongarse mientras Donald Trump permanezca en la Casa Blanca.

Trump vuelve a arremeter contra Canadá

El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, quien permaneció en silencio durante el sábado, retomó sus críticas contra Ottawa durante la madrugada del domingo y volvió a denunciar lo que considera una “continua discriminación” y un “trato desigual” hacia el comercio estadounidense.

“¡¡¡Canadá quiere los beneficios de ser un estado, sin serlo!!!”, escribió Trump en Truth Social, donde también acusó al país vecino de imponer durante años elevados aranceles a los agricultores estadounidenses.

Un día antes, el representante comercial de Estados Unidos, Jamieson Greer, había señalado que no existen nuevas conversaciones previstas con Canadá y describió los aranceles como “contramedidas” ante lo que calificó como un año de represalias contra las políticas comerciales de la administración Trump.

Las medidas también han generado críticas dentro de Estados Unidos. Gobernadores demócratas como Gavin Newsom, de California, y Abigail Spanberger, de Virginia, cuestionaron la imposición de nuevos aranceles contra Canadá, al que describieron como un socio comercial clave y aliado histórico.

Ambos advirtieron sobre las posibles consecuencias de una guerra comercial para los productores estadounidenses.

Por su parte, el exvicepresidente estadounidense Mike Pence, quien ocupó el cargo durante el primer mandato de Trump entre 2017 y 2021, advirtió este domingo que la disputa comercial entre Estados Unidos y Canadá representa nuevos riesgos para la economía estadounidense en momentos en que sus consumidores ya enfrentan costos elevados.

news.title: Trump takes starring role at Washington's IndyCar debut
news.text: US President Donald Trump rode a ceremonial lap in his armored limousine and waved the green flag to start Sunday's IndyCar race through the streets of Washington, capping celebrations of America's 250th birthday..Trump, who created the Freedom 250 Grand Prix by executive order for the United States anniversary commemoration, had a prime view of the 250-mile (400km) spectacle as open-wheel cars roared past iconic landmarks at speeds up to 185 mph (298 km/h). ."It has turned out to be bigger than we ever thought possible," Trump told race telecaster Fox. "The track is wonderful.".American Kyle Kirkwood won his seventh career IndyCar race after two hours 40mins, 42.9548secs, beating Denmark's Christian Lundgaard by 3.09 seconds with Australian Will Power third.."You can't even put it into words. This is incredible," Kirkwood said. "I'm almost in tears. This is a big moment for us. A big moment for America.".Trump greeted IndyCar series owner Roger Penske, 89, and the seven Indianapolis 500 winners in the field of 25 before the 147-lap event began, telling the racers, "Good luck, do well, have fun."."Roger told me they had been trying to do it for 20 years and when Trump came along they got it done," the 80-year-old president said..Power was stunned to meet Trump, saying "Shaking President Trump's hand, it was pretty crazy.."For me from a small town in Australia to be talking to an American President is surreal... then getting behind the wheel and racing.".'Big fan'.Trump and First Lady Melania Trump slowly took a pre-race lap around the 1.7-mile layout inside his armored limousine known as "The Beast," weaving around such landmarks such as the Washington Monument, US Capitol and museums.."The president wanted to do this. He's a big fan. We wanted to be part of the 250th anniversary," Penske said. "This is an iconic race.".IndyCar and Penske Racing paid most of the $35 million cost to stage the race, with Penske president and Freedom 250 chairman Bud Denker saying 215,000 people attended two days of events..Pre-race flyovers included ones by a stealth bomber and Air Force One, with air traffic paused at nearby Reagan National Airport for the race..Trump waved the green flag at the start-finish line in front of the US Capitol to start the race..Trump has taken major roles in other events to celebrate the anniversary of the July 4, 1776, signing of the Declaration of Independence -- a document housed inside the race course at the National Archives..Trump helmed an Ultimate Fighting Championship bout in a cage on the White House lawn in June..Trump's vision for Washington also includes construction projects like the White House ballroom and a proposed triumphal arch..Kirkwood escaped a tense moment on a late restart when New Zealand's Scott McLaughlin crashed trying to pass him, then led to the finish.."It was something very special. I will cherish this moment for a very long time," Kirkwood said.."I don't know if we're ever going to have another chance, I hope we do, but this was awesome. A dream come true.".Added Power: "When I pulled in at the end, you see President Trump still watching, so the race must have been engaging. That's great to see.".- 'A surreal day' -.Mario Andretti, the 86-year-old US racing legend whose 1969 Indy 500-winning car is in the Smithsonian museum, was impressed.."Fabulous to be here. This event is really amazing," Andretti said. .IndyCar will consider returning, with Penske saying, "We'll talk about it. We'll have to meet next week.".Denker called it "a surreal day" sitting with Trump, saying the president wants the race to return for five more years and his wife has 2027 expectations.."Melania on the way out said, 'We look forward to seeing you next year,'" Denker said. "The pressure is on. The First Lady is involved.".Denker noted walls from the course will be stored nearby, and the "investment is already made in the walls and some infrastructure." ."The decision would be up to us. I'd be concerned about raising the same kind of revenue we did this year."
news.summary: Trump set for starring role at Washington's debut IndyCar race
